text:
Both summaries are accurate on the substance. They give the correct release date and correctly describe the Classic CSV removal: imports break because the new format has different column names and a separate GST column. Both point to the help article and correctly state that Android 9 gets no further updates. Neither adds that the app keeps working on Android 9, but neither says anything false about it. A's "See the help article... before updating" is sensible advice drawn from the source. Grouping bug fixes under "Improvements" is only a loose label, not an error.

On keeping what the manager needs, both flag the CSV breakage as the key action item. A leads with it, which suits a busy reader. B opens with features instead. A also mentions the ATO-aligned GST rounding, which matters for compliance. B instead uses words on lesser details such as per-client reminder wording and beta access.

On the explicit constraint, A comes to about 116 words and stays under the 120-word limit. B comes to about 124 words and exceeds it. That is a direct failure to follow the instruction.

A is accurate, puts the important point first, and meets the length limit. B is accurate but over the limit.

Verdict: A
